6. Mr Moudud Ahmed submits that it is conceivable that a man just disappears and police are unable to find him out. He, however, refers to the case of S. Mohsin Sharif vs The Government of the Peoples of Republic of Bangladesh, 27 DLR 186 and Abdul Latif Mirza vs The Government of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh 31 DLR (AD) 1. We shall discuss the cases mentioned above later in the body of the judgment. 

 15. Mr Moudud Ahmed supplementing Mr Khondker Mahbub Hossain refers to the case of S Mohsin Sharif vs The Government of the People s Republic of Bangladesh, 27 DLR 186. In this case one Shahjahan, a young man of 18 years' old was arrested on 28-12-1973 by the Cantonment Artillery Headquarters, Dhaka by Surgent Riazuddin, He was then taken to the Ramna Police Station and a GD Entry dated 28-12-73 was made showing his arrest under section 54 CrPC. Soon thereafter Major Shahed of Field Intelligence Unit (FlU), Dhaka Cantonment asked the Officer-in-Charge of Ramna Police Station to hand over Shahjahan to Subeder Major Hafizuddin of the Jatiya Rakkhi Bahini (JRB) and -accordingly Rakkhi Bahini took Shahjahan under its custody and took him to. Sher-e-Bangla Rakkhi Bahini Headquarters and kept him there till 2-1-74. The brother of Shahjahan talked to Shahjahan at Rakkhi Bahirii Head Quarters on 30-12-73 and 2-1-74 Shahjahan complained to him that he had been inhumanly tortured by Rakkhi Bahini men. Ultimately, Shahjahan was not traced out and his brother made an earnest search but did not find him out. It is said that Shahjahan was made a confession and led the Rakkhi Bahini party to a spot near Mohammadpur where from a number of arms were recovered. On 28-12-1973 at 3-00 am, Shahjahan again led the party to another place near Rayer Bazar Mondir and entered into a by- lane and eluding the party suddenly ran away and escaped. All attempts to re-arrest him failed. 

 18. Mr Moudud Ahmed, learned Advocate also refers to the case of Abdul Latif Mirza vs Government of Bangladesh, 31 DLR (AD) 1. In this case the detenu Abdul Latif Mirza challenged his detention by writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. The Deputy Commissioner, Pabna by his order dated 22-4-1974, under section 3 of the Special Powers Act, detained him for a period of thirty days and thereafter the Government on 24-5-1974, passed under clause (a) of section 3(1) of the Special Powers Act, an order of detention until further orders, on the ground, that it was satisfied that the order was necessary for the purpose of preventing him from doing any prejudicial act. The High Court Division discharged the Rule. In such back ground of the case, the Appellate Division quoting the decision taken in the case of Federal Court of India in the case of Basanta Chandra Ghose vs Emperor, AIR 1945 FC 18, the case of Narayan Singh Nathuram vs State of Punjab AIR 1952 (SC) 106, the case of Ram Narayan Singh vs The State of Delhi AIR 1952 (SC) 277, the case of Sharafuddin Ahmed vs Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs (1975) 27 DLR 658 held that the detention of the appellant was not sustainable in law and allowed the appeal. This case relates to the detention of the detenu. The facts and circumstances of the case referred to above and the facts and circumstances of the case in hand are not similar an identical. Therefore.the principle expounded in the case referred to above does not apply in the facts and circumstances of the case in hand.
